author: Ash

copy.intro: You've found the Fear of God Classic Hoodie, sun-faded and made in the USA, then seen the $595 price tag. Maybe you'll pay that and just want a different name on the hood. Or maybe you want the washed, heavy look for far less. These 13 brands all sell hoodies to the US. Some charge just as much, and others cost a third of it. The closest to Fear of God's price come first.

bodies.nahmias:
NAHMIAS is the closest thing to Fear of God's sun-faded LA fleece, and its prices start far lower. The Miracle Academy Hoodie in Black Sunfade ($215) is 100% cotton French terry, made in Los Angeles and cut oversized.

Doni Nahmias started the label in Los Angeles in 2018, mixing skate, basketball, surf and hip-hop codes. So expect patches, crystals and team logos where Fear of God prints old athletic lockups. At the top, the Ollie Hoodie ($650) and the Flower Groms Zip Up Hoodie ($695) cost what a Fear of God Classic does. Every hoodie comes in S to XXL, and most go to XXXL.

The return window is the catch. You get 10 days, five fewer than Fear of God gives, and the label is on you. For more breathing room, Acne Studios gives you 14 days and pays for the return.
bodies.acne-studios:
Acne Studios is where to spend Fear of God money if you want the shipping and duties handled for you. Its Fleece logo hoodie ($730) is organic cotton fleece, piece-dyed for a slightly worn, vintage look. That's the same idea as Fear of God's sunfade, from a Stockholm fashion house.

US orders usually ship from inside the US with tariffs and duties paid, and express delivery is free on every order. Returns are free too, within 14 days. The Sprayed zip hoodie ($860) is the other style at full price.

Check the size list before you fall for one. The cut is relaxed and unisex, from XXXS to XXL, so it stops a size short of Fear of God's XXXL. If you need that bigger size, AMIRI carries it on every men's hoodie.
bodies.rick-owens:
Rick Owens is where to go if Fear of God's prices don't put you off and you want a less classic shape. Every full-price hoodie in its US store is from the DRKSHDW line, starting with the Tommy Hustler Hoodie ($655) in medium-weight cotton jersey.

Budget closer to $1,000 for most of the range. The Mountain Hoodie ($965) comes in heavy jersey, the Collage Gimp Hoodie ($920) is cropped, and the Peter Hoodie tops out at $1,220 in an oversized fit. Colors run black, dust, grape and mineral, against Fear of God's browns, ivory and sky.

It has five US stores, including Los Angeles and New York, so you can try one on first. That helps, because an online order gives you just 10 days to send it back. Check your state too. Shoppers in a dozen states, California and New York among them, pay import duties on top.
bodies.amiri:
AMIRI is the other LA label that charges what Fear of God does, then keeps going. The MA Core Logo Hoodie ($650) is its cheapest at full price, a little under Fear of God's Baseball Club Half Zip Hoodie ($695).

Above that, you're paying for decoration. The Multi Bandana OS Zip Hoodie ($1,150) carries a sun-faded bandana print, and the crystal and stud zip hoodies reach $1,590. Every men's style goes up to XXXL, the same top size as Fear of God's classics.

Standard US shipping is free, and so are returns within the US. But the window is 10 days, so don't leave the box sealed for long. If $650 is your ceiling rather than your starting point, NAHMIAS sells vintage-washed LA hoodies from $215.
bodies.raised-by-wolves:
Raised by Wolves is the pick for a hoodie nobody else will have. Its Wild Ones Hoodie ($250) is made in Canada from hand-selected deadstock heavyweight cotton jersey, and each one is a one-of-one, listed in a single size.

That changes how you shop. You're choosing a piece, not a color, so filter by your size first and see what's left. The label started in Ottawa in 2008, rooted in graphic design, and now makes sportswear and outerwear for Canada's climate. A Wild Ones hoodie costs less than half a Fear of God Classic.

The catch is a big one for US buyers. It doesn't accept international returns at all, so a US order is final. If you want a returnable hoodie near this price, A-COLD-WALL* gives you 28 days.
bodies.a-cold-wall:
A-COLD-WALL* is the one to try if you like Fear of God's washed fleece but not its price. The Bescott Hoodie ($238) is heavyweight loopback cotton with a garment soft wash, in bone, garnet or onyx.

The London label says its clothes come out of fabric and material study, and the hoodies show it in small details. The Bescott has contrast twin-needle stitching, and the Millbank Hoodie ($265) has piped seams across the front. For the lowest price, start with the Balmore Logo Hoodie ($170).

Prices show in dollars, and you get 28 days to request a return, nearly twice Fear of God's 15. Email first, though, because parcels sent back without an approved request are refused. Sizes vary by style, with some stopping at XXL and others reaching 3XL.
bodies.represent:
If fleece weight is what you're paying Fear of God for, Represent gets you there for less. Most of its hoodies state 480gsm or more, and the Owners Club Hoodie ($200) is roughly a third of a Fear of God Classic.

The range runs from $140 to $315, so there's room to trade up without getting near $395. It's a British label with a flagship in Los Angeles as well as London and Manchester, and US orders leave from inside the country, with no shipping charge over $175.

The 14-day return window is one day short of Fear of God's, with $9 taken off for the US label. If you'd rather a British label that folds duties into the price, Cole Buxton does.
bodies.cole-buxton:
Cole Buxton is the pick if you like the old athletic look of a Fear of God Classic but want less branding on it. The London label says it set out to make collections that weren't loud or aggressively branded. Its Signature Hoodie ($187) has just a puff-printed logo, front and back.

The CB Sportswear Hoodie, also $187, is the one with the bigger back print, in 440gsm brushed cotton jersey that's pre-shrunk and garment washed. That wash is its nearest link to Fear of God's sunfaded fleece. Zipped versions go to $234.

Delivery is where it gets expensive. You'd need $340 in your basket for free shipping, so a single hoodie won't get there, though US duties are already included at checkout. Returns last 14 days at your own cost.
bodies.john-elliott:
John Elliott is the LA label to look at for independent luxury at about a third of Fear of God's price. It started in 2012, a year before Fear of God. At full price it sells one hoodie, the Beach Hoodie 2 ($198), cut relaxed and a little cropped from 100% cotton French terry.

The Beach Hoodie 2 is made in Peru rather than the USA, the main difference from a Fear of God Classic. Sizes run XS to XXXL, matching it. And US shipping is free on any order, with no $100 minimum to reach.

You can see it in person at its West Hollywood and New York stores. You have 14 days to send it back, minus a $7 label fee, which is exactly what Fear of God deducts. For more styles at a similar price, Noah or Cole Buxton have them.
bodies.noah:
Noah suits you if you care where a hoodie is made, which Fear of God's USA-made classics suggest you do. Every full-price hoodie it sells is Canadian-made, in brushed-back fleece that's all cotton. The Heavyweight Zip-Up Hoodie ($228) uses 15 oz fabric, the heaviest of its hoodies.

It's a New York menswear label from Brendon Babenzien and Estelle Bailey-Babenzien, and it sells itself on clothing made responsibly. The Core Classic Hoodie ($168) is the cheapest way in, less than a third of a Fear of God Classic.

Two things to know. The 14-day full-refund clock starts when the order ships, not when it arrives. And full-price hoodie stock is thin. If you'd rather choose from a deeper range at this price, Represent has far more styles.
bodies.fear-of-god-essentials:
Fear of God Essentials is the obvious move, since it's the company's own second line, sold in the same store for a fraction of the price. Hoodies run $150 to $195, so even the top of the range costs less than half of Fear of God's cheapest $395 collaboration hoodie.

The Phillies Raglan Half Zip Sport Hoodie ($175) is the nearest thing to the main line's Baseball Club Half Zip ($695), at a quarter of the price. Fleece weights run from 380 to 520gsm, and many styles reach XXXL.

Shipping matches the main line, free once you pass $100 in the lower 48. Returns don't. The main line gives you 15 days, but Essentials is final sale with no exceptions, so settle on a size before you order.
bodies.born-x-raised:
Born x Raised trades Fear of God's own lockups for licensed team logos, and it's LA-based too. It's been going since 2013, the same year as Fear of God, and its hoodies run $120 to $200, most of them around $140.

The NFL Crest Hoodies ($140) and MLB Moneyball Hoodies ($180) are the draw. Its own Llorona Zip-Up Hoodie ($200) is the priciest. Sizes go from S to 3XL, the same top size as Fear of God's classics, but it starts a size later.

Read the policy first. Every sale is final, apart from damage or a production fault. For a returnable hoodie around this price, Represent's start at $140 with 14 days to change your mind.
bodies.madhappy:
Madhappy makes the heavyweight LA hoodie you can still send back. The Classics Fleece Hoodie ($175) is its core style, heavyweight cotton fleece in a relaxed unisex fit, made in Los Angeles, in more than 20 colors.

That puts it close to Fear of God's classics in how it's built, heavy cotton fleece produced in the US, at under a third of the price. The return window is 30 days, twice Fear of God's, and there's no $12 deduction if you choose store credit or an exchange over a refund.

Sizes stop at XXL, though, one short of Fear of God. A single Classics hoodie falls short of the $200 free-shipping bar, so it ships for $5. If you'd rather try it on, there are stores in West Hollywood, New York and Malibu.

closing.heading: How to choose
closing.body:
Start with how much of that $595 you're willing to spend. If you'd pay it anyway, NAHMIAS and AMIRI keep the LA vintage-wash look, while Rick Owens trades it for DRKSHDW's odder cuts. Acne Studios is the one that covers duties and returns for you.

Between $170 and $315, it's about the fabric. Represent and Cole Buxton list heavy fleece weights, and A-COLD-WALL* gives you 28 days to decide. Under $200, Madhappy is the LA-made pick you can return, and John Elliott ships free at any order size.

Essentials and Born x Raised are cheap too, but both are final sale, and so are Raised by Wolves' one-of-ones for US buyers. So if you might change your mind, cross those three off first.

faqs.q: Is Essentials cheaper than Fear of God?
faqs.a: Yes, by a long way. Essentials hoodies cost $150 to $195, while main-line Fear of God hoodies run $395 to $695. Both sell through fearofgod.com, but every Essentials piece is final sale.

faqs.q: Is Fear of God a luxury brand?
faqs.a: Yes. It calls its view an American take on luxury, and its main-line hoodies cost $395 to $695, made in the USA from heavyweight cotton fleece. Its wool pants go past $1,000.

Jerry Lorenzo started Fear of God in 2013. It's an American label that ships orders from its distribution center in Los Angeles and sells both the main line and the cheaper Essentials line in its own store.
